q: What is the difference between a future method and a Queueable class?
alt: Queueable vs future method, when do you use which?
Why would you choose Queueable over @future?
Can you chain future methods, and what is the alternative?
a: Both run Apex in the background, but Queueable is the more flexible one. A future method only accepts primitive parameters, you cannot monitor it, and you cannot chain it. A Queueable class can take complex types like sObjects or custom objects, it returns a job Id so you can track it in AsyncApexJob, and it can enqueue another job from its execute method to chain work. I use future only for quick, simple callouts, and Queueable for anything that needs state, chaining or monitoring.
points: Future: static void method, primitives only, no job Id, no chaining
Queueable: complex parameters, job Id for monitoring, chaining from execute
Both need Database.AllowsCallouts / callout=true for callouts
